The Saint John Board of Police Commissioners (the “Commission”) is seeking a forward-looking police leader to serve as its next Chief of Police.
 Reporting to and receiving direction from the Commission, the Chief of Police serves as the Chief Executive Officer of the Police Force and the senior law enforcement leader for the community.
 The Chief will lead a police service focused on effective, lawful, ethical and community-centred policing. You will provide visible leadership across the organization, champion public trust and community partnerships, and connect the Commission’s strategic direction to the decisions and actions of members across the Force.
 As Chief, you will lead and administer the Force in accordance with the Police Act, provincial policing standards, Commission policies and the Commission’s strategic direction. You will be accountable for organizational performance, professional conduct, public confidence and community safety outcomes.
 The Role
 As Chief of Police, you will maintain an effective, transparent working relationship with the Commission and comply with its lawful direction and instructions. You will develop, implement and oversee professional police procedures and ensure members carry out their duties professionally, fairly and in compliance with applicable law, standards, policies and collective agreements.
 You will report regularly to the Commission on operations, organizational performance, progress against the strategic plan, policy compliance, risks, emerging issues and matters requiring Commission awareness or action. You will maintain accountability for the performance, conduct, professionalism and communications of the Force and its members.
 In leading the Force, you will:
 ·   Champion an inclusive community policing service-delivery model built on public trust, community partnerships and problem solving, grounded in the principle that “police are the public and the public are police.”
 ·   Create and sustain an inclusive, participatory working environment for sworn and civilian members, full- and part-time employees, contract workers and volunteers.
 ·   Provide visible leadership across the organization so members understand strategic priorities and how their decisions and actions contribute to community safety and well-being.
 ·   Promote a culture of openness to new ideas, creativity, innovation, teamwork, learning, accountability and continuous improvement.
 ·   Convey a positive and credible image of the Police Force to the public, community partners, stakeholders and media.
 ·   Model integrity, authenticity, transparency, professionalism, fairness and respect in all decisions, communications and relationships.
 Organizational Leadership
 You will manage and direct the Police Force to meet or exceed applicable policing standards while taking into account local conditions, evolving risks and community expectations.
 You will prepare and propose annual budget options to the Commission, identifying anticipated operational impacts and alignment with strategic priorities and objectives. You will directly supervise, develop and mentor Deputy Chief(s), senior leaders and other direct reports, sworn and civilian.
 You will establish and oversee fair, unbiased and transparent systems for hiring, development, supervision, evaluation, recognition, compensation, promotion and discipline. You will prepare the organization for the future through succession planning and the ongoing development of middle and senior managers.
 You will build and maintain constructive relationships with labour associations, municipal partners, community organizations, partner agencies, provincial bodies and policing counterparts. You will also participate in the City’s Public Safety Committee meetings.
 The Ideal Candidate
 You are an experienced and respected police executive who understands the opportunities and challenges of leading a small or medium-sized police service. Ideally, you have served as a Chief of Police or Deputy Chief, or held a comparable senior executive leadership role, within a small or medium-sized Canadian municipal police service or detachment.
 You understand that leadership in a police service in a regional city requires both strategic perspective and a visible, hands-on leadership presence. You are comfortable working directly with the Commission, senior leaders, members of the Force, municipal partners, labour associations, community organizations and other policing and public-safety partners.
 You have demonstrated your ability to work with partners to reduce crime, improve community safety and well-being, and respond to complex public-safety challenges. You have successfully managed in a unionized environment and bring experience with large operational budgets, financial planning and controls, procurement, resource allocation, and related financial and administrative responsibilities.
 You have a proven record of building trust within diverse communities and across all ranks and employee groups within a police organization. You are a visible and credible leader who communicates effectively, develops people and builds strong organizational teams.
 You understand modern independent civilian police governance and oversight, including the Commission’s role as employer, supervisor and strategic governance body. You know how to build an effective relationship with a civilian police commission while respecting the distinct responsibilities and accountabilities of the Chief and the Commission.
 You are comfortable navigating uncertainty and taking accountability for matters you can influence, not only those you directly control. You bring adaptive leadership, systems thinking and complex problem-solving skills, together with an inclusive orientation, empathy, innovation and a commitment to continuous improvement.
 You will bring the judgement and leadership experience to guide the Force through its next chapter while maintaining the trust of its members, the Commission and the community it serves.
 Working in the Community
  The Chief works primarily in an office and meeting environment and regularly attends Commission meetings, internal meetings, public events, community forums and partner-agency engagements.
 As Chief, you will maintain a visible and accessible presence with members of the Force, community partners and the public. You will maintain required police qualifications and may travel outside the jurisdiction for professional meetings, networking and related duties.
 The Chief is expected to reside locally and to be available for significant operational, public-safety or organizational matters as required.
 You will ideally bring post-secondary education in a field relevant to policing, community safety and well-being, public administration, leadership, law, criminology or a related discipline.
 Experience leading organizational transformation, equity-focused initiatives, community partnerships and modern police-service delivery is also preferred.

ABOUT THIS ROLE

As Ashby’s first Demo Engineer, you’ll own the systems that make our demo environments reliable, current, and tailored — the infrastructure the entire go-to-market team leans on to show Ashby at its best. Today, AEs and SEs maintain and configure their own demo accounts by hand. That doesn’t scale: reps lose selling time, demos drift out of date, and every new product release widens the gap between what Ashby can do and what we can actually show live. Your job is to close that gap.

This is a net-new role. Right now, the work is split between ad hoc effort and a new set of disposable demo templates the Internal Platform team is building. You’ll own the layer on top of that foundation — customizing and extending those templates, generating realistic demo data, tailoring environments for specific verticals and new markets, and making sure every feature is demoable before it ships. You’ll sit within Solutions Engineering, reporting to the Global Head of Solutions Engineering, and partner closely with Internal Platform and Product teams.

Your work will be split roughly 70/30: about 70% owning, customizing, and extending the demo template system and the data and content inside it, and about 30% running demo readiness as a program — release readiness, documentation, and enablement so the GTM team always has current, credible demos to work with.

The best person for this job is genuinely hands-on technical — working with internal tools and configuration files, using APIs, and general data preparation — who gets energy from building leverage for a whole team rather than fixing one demo at a time.




YOU COULD BE A GREAT FIT IF:

 - 🛠 You’re comfortable working in JSON, calling REST / developer APIs, using AI tools, and scripting to configure and customize environments.

 - 🏗 You’re a builder, not just an operator. You get energy from creating systems and tooling that make a whole team more effective over time.

 - 🎥 You care deeply about demo quality. You understand what makes a product demo land, and you’re thoughtful about data realism and the narrative a demo needs to support.

 - 🧠 You have strong product intuition and can learn a deeply configurable product quickly, understanding how the different pieces connect.

 - 🔁 You have an iterative mindset. You like testing what works, refining over time, and improving based on what you learn from the field.

 - 🧩 You’re a systems thinker who would rather standardize and automate than manually repeat the same setup.

 - ⚡ You’re comfortable with ambiguity and enjoy a 0→1 role where the infrastructure is still being built around you.

Everyone can run a search campaign. Almost nobody can tell you whether it worked. 
 That is the whole job.
 Google will happily show you a 6x ROAS built almost entirely out of people who already knew your client's name. It will auto apply assets you did not ask for. It will report a number that makes a client feel great and tells you nothing about whether you grew the business.
 So we do not hire people to manage Google Ads. We hire marketers who can tell the difference between demand they created and demand they harvested, and who can prove it to a client's face.
 At Sweat Pants Agency we work with around 50 DTC and eCommerce brands, 20 to 25 of them on paid media. We spend $6 to $9M a month on Meta and $1 to $2M a month on Google. We are the only agency behind two INC #1 fastest growing brands, both from zero.
 You would own a set of our Google accounts end to end.
 Here is what "end to end" actually means.
 You are the account manager. We do not have any.  You talk to the client directly. You write the updates, you run the calls, and you defend the call you made. The reason we do it this way is ownership. When you are the person answering for the account, it is your result, not somebody else's summary of your result.
 You own the whole funnel, not the campaign.  Feed and Merchant Center, search and Shopping and PMax, Demand Gen and YouTube, the landing page, and the conversion tracking underneath all of it. If the feed is why Shopping is starving, that is yours. If the page is why the clicks do not convert, that is yours too. Our team ships advertorials, comparison pages, and PDPs in Claude Code, deploys them to Vercel, points a subdomain at them, and tests them live before anything touches the client's Shopify theme.
 You are expected to have an opinion about attribution and to defend it.  We optimize to NC-CPA and NC-ROAS, not blended and not last click. We have turned brand search off to see what actually shifts to organic. We run geo holdouts. If a campaign is not incremental, we would rather know than keep the number.
 You can live anywhere.  We are remote and we hire worldwide. The one hard requirement is that you can take client calls during US Eastern business hours, because you are the client's point of contact. The rest of your day is yours. Nobody here is on a time clock. We judge you on output.
 If you want a lane, a ticket queue, and a scope document, this is a bad fit and we will both know it fast.
 If you want to own the whole picture and be judged on whether the number moved, keep reading.
 What the job looks like 
 Own a set of DTC accounts  as the strategist, the buyer, and the client's direct point of contact. Budgets run from $5k/mo to well into six figures a month.
 Own the client relationship.  There is no account manager between you and them. You present the results, the plan, and the reasoning, and you are the one who answers when something is not working.
 Audit before you touch anything.  Every account we take over gets a real review first: campaign and ad group structure, keywords versus search terms, negatives, bidding strategy per campaign type, impression share, feed health, landing pages, audiences, and conversion tracking. Then a Loom walking the client through what you found. That Loom is how we sell and it is how we keep people.
 Run brand and non brand as different businesses.  Brand is mostly assisted conversion and it usually belongs on target impression share, not target CPA. Non brand is where the growth is and where the waste is. Report them separately or you are reporting nothing.
 Know what PMax is actually doing.  The most common mistake we see is optimizing PMax against an incremental CAC when half the volume inside it is branded. If you cannot separate those two, you cannot set a target.
 Keep Google's automation on a leash.  Auto applied recommendations, auto applied assets, and auto created sitelinks have cost our clients real money. We audit for them on a schedule.
 Own the feed.  Merchant Center hygiene, product titles, disapprovals, promotions, and what the feed does to Shopping and PMax delivery.
 Own the tracking.  GA4, GTM, Shopify goal imports versus a raw Google Ads tag, enhanced conversions, offline conversion imports for the lead gen accounts. When the numbers do not reconcile, you are the one who finds out why.
 Diagnose the bottleneck, then go fix it.  Creative, offer, AOV, landing page, checkout, tracking. Nobody is going to reassign it to another team.
 Build the things the account needs.  Landing pages, scripts, reporting, whatever removes the constraint. We are heavy AI users and we expect you to build, not just prompt.
 You are a fit if 
 You have done this with real money.  Hands on Google Ads at meaningful spend on DTC and eCommerce, with results you can walk us through: CPA, ROAS, revenue, and what you actually changed to get them. Shopping and PMax specifically, not just search.
 You are fluent in the whole stack , not one campaign type. Search, Shopping, PMax, Demand Gen, YouTube, Merchant Center, GA4, GTM. Bing is a nice to have.
 You are AI native, and you build.  This is a requirement, not a bonus. You should already be using Claude or equivalent as a working tool rather than a novelty, and you should be able to build and ship a landing page with it.
 You can communicate your ideas in English at a native or near native level.  You will be in front of clients constantly. You need to explain your thinking clearly, sell an idea on its merits, push back when a client is about to force the account into mediocrity, and raise a problem before it becomes a fire. This matters as much as anything else on this list.
 You are skeptical of your own numbers.  You would rather run the holdout than protect the dashboard.
 You can work US Eastern business hours for client calls.  Where you live is up to you.
 Bonus: you have built or operated your own Shopify store, or you have run Meta at spend too.
 You are not a fit if 
 "That was not my role" is in your vocabulary. It is the fastest way to end an interview here. If the feed was the problem on an account you ran, you should have done something about the feed.
 You want to be told what to do this week.
 You need a ticketing system to know what matters.
 You quote blended ROAS as if it settles the question.
 Why this role is exciting 
 This is not a maintenance job. You would have real influence over how we run Google across the agency.
 You will work on real brands with real budgets. We test aggressively. We learn quickly. We build frameworks that scale.
 You get trust on day one. You get a lot of autonomy. Some people thrive with it. You will get feedback fast either way, and if you make it through the first 30 days you will probably be here for a long time. Our retention on this team is very good and that is not an accident.
 You will grow into senior strategy. We want people who want more responsibility. If you perform, you will grow.

Our Mission
Swapcard is the leading AI-powered event platform designed to drive revenue growth and foster meaningful connections at in-person and hybrid events. We recognize the importance of teamwork in successful events; that's why Swapcard is fueled by a team of innovators who are passionate about helping organizers build future-proof events.

Our Vision
At Swapcard, we believe in the power of meaningful connections.  This belief fuels our commitment to pioneering modern solutions that empower organizers to create engaging event experiences.
 Guided by our commitment to excellence and collaboration, we aim to redefine the landscape of event technology, setting new standards for engagement, accessibility, and impact.

Our Beliefs
At Swapcard, diversity is at the core of our success. With 42 nationalities represented among our 180+ team members, we champion diversity as a catalyst for creativity, collaboration, and unparalleled innovation.

We believe that by embracing a multitude of backgrounds, cultures, and viewpoints, we can truly understand and cater to the needs of our global community of event organizers and participants.
Our full remote opportunities empower our team to thrive, no matter where they are in the world, fostering a culture of flexibility and inclusion.


Swapcard is the platform behind some of the largest trade shows, conferences and association events in the world, and our Customer Account Managers own the relationship with the organisers who run them.
We're investing in the next stage of that relationship: growth. Our clients don't run one event — they run portfolios, sometimes more than a hundred events, each with its own calendar, its own team and its own decision points. Growing alongside them at that scale is a discipline in its own right: a repeatable motion, a shared qualification standard, and a rhythm built around the client's event cycle rather than our fiscal quarters.
The CAM team sits inside our Customer organisation, alongside Solution Design, Implementation and Support. Whoever leads it works shoulder to shoulder with the teams that scope, deliver and support everything the CAMs sell.
Today, two team leads run the CAM function reporting directly into leadership. As we accelerate the growth motion, we want a single senior leader to bring that work together — someone who builds the playbook with the team, coaches them on live calls, and holds a clear analytical view of where the opportunity sits. That's the role.

Scope: Portfolio. 500+ events across our installed base, run by organisers whose portfolios range from a handful of events to well over a hundred.
 Team. 10+ people spread between the US and Europe. Two CAM leads report to you directly who run the rest of the team.
 Target. +20% growth on the installed base, delivered through an account-based strategy.
 Two levers. Higher penetration of each client's event portfolio, and upsell of digital add-ons and additional modules on the events already running on Swapcard.
 Mandate. Renew, expand, and prevent churn and downsell.
Responsibilities: Lead the CAM team. You'll lead the Customer Account Manager teams across North America and EMEA through your Strategic Account Managers and Team Leads, and set the standard for the wider CAM organisation.
 Own the number. Carry the +20% growth target and build the account-based plan behind it: which accounts, which events inside their portfolio, which modules, in which order, and what has to be true for each to land.
 Protect the base. Churn and downsell are rarely a surprise to someone who is looking. Build the early-warning discipline, get ahead of the competitive and budget conversations, and treat renewal as a managed motion rather than a date on a calendar.
 Build the growth motion. Shape the qualification standard the team works to, the criteria that let an opportunity enter the forecast, and the discipline that keeps the picture current. You'll define what counts as good evidence and help the team hold to it consistently.
 Coach on live calls. Join discovery calls alongside the CAMs, debrief together afterwards, and help shape how the next conversation goes. This is where most of the value of the role sits. We expect a lot of hands-on coaching.
 Own the KPIs and the weekly rhythm. Activity, contact creation, qualification progress, outreach, forecast. You'll build the pack, read it before anyone else does, and bring attention to where it's needed early rather than explaining it late.
 Run the enablement programme. Build it, run it, and certify the team on real accounts. Enablement here is a line responsibility that sits with you, not something handed off.
 Align the system. Marketing, Revenue Ops, Sales Enablement, Solution Design and Product. An account-based motion only works when those move together, and making that happen is your job rather than someone else's favour.
 Partner with Marketing on account-based campaigns. Work as Marketing's counterpart rather than a requester — personas, account selection, sequencing against each client's event cycle, and an honest, shared read of what worked.
 Influence the roadmap. Bring structured insight from the account base back to Product: what's blocking expansion, what competitors are winning on, what the industry is moving toward. Opinions with evidence behind them, early enough to shape what gets built.
 Keep the data trustworthy. Account context, classification, CRM hygiene. A stale account brief is worth a real conversation with the team, because the whole motion depends on the data being sound.
 Escalate what matters, early. Surface what stands between a client and a decision — product, commercial terms or timing — with the evidence attached and early enough for the decision to change the outcome.
What we're looking for: A growth builder in SaaS. You've delivered growth of this order inside an existing SaaS customer base — qualification, cadence, forecast, expansion pipeline — not just managed a book of accounts well. No event industry experience needed. We can teach you the industry; we can't teach the motion.
 Account-based, in practice. You've led, structured and implemented an account-based strategy for a SaaS business, with Marketing alongside you rather than downstream of you.
 A complex seller. Long sales cycles, several business units inside the same account, top-down and bottom-up in parallel. You know how to find the blocker — budget, politics, product, timing — name it, and work it rather than wait it out.
 An account manager who became a strong coach. You've carried a portfolio yourself, and you develop people in the moment: you can hear what's missing in a discovery call and help the CAM get there themselves next time.
 A leader of distributed teams. You've managed managers and a fully distributed team across time zones, ideally between North America and Europe, and you set a standard others want to work to.
 A systems thinker with an engineer's mindset. You think in processes, inputs and feedback loops. Strong analytically, fluent in data at portfolio level (CRM, complex spreadsheets), and very organised. Evidence, not instinct, is how you make and defend a call.
 Direct. Straight to the point with your team and with clients. Comfortable in difficult customer conversations, willing to push back, and not afraid to ask the hard question early rather than discover the answer late.
 Composed under pressure. You do your best work in a fast-moving, high-stakes commercial environment, and you keep the team steady when timelines compress around clients' event dates.
 A clear, credible communicator. You report upward without being chased and you partner naturally across functions.
 Useful, not essential: experience in events, media or B2B marketplaces, where the buying unit is an event and its date sets the deadline.
 Experience: 7 to 10+ years in account management, customer success or commercial roles, including at least 3 managing managers or a distributed team.
 Language: fluent English. French is a plus, not a requirement.

 Student Orientation

This role sits at the intersection of product strategy, cross-functional leadership, and agile execution — requiring someone who can both shape long-term direction and deliver with precision.
 We are the team that builds solutions that protect our customer’s Auth0 environments. Our group delivers features such as attack protection, bot detection, adaptive MFA, identity security for AI Agents and related analytics / insights on the effectiveness of our solutions in thwarting attacks from bad actors.
 The ideal candidate brings direct, hands-on experience in agentic security product management, with a deep understanding of how AI agents are built, orchestrated, and secured.  Score the clinical reasoning quality of benchmark items: vignette accuracy and completeness, whether the vignette gives the answer away, answer correctness and gradeability, and trap quality;

 Nous recherchons un(e) spécialiste des pratiques de gestion de produit, doté(e) d’un esprit pratique, pour mettre en œuvre et opérationnaliser les pratiques, les processus et les outils permettant à la gestion de produit de fonctionner de manière cohérente et efficace à grande échelle.
 Votre rôle consistera à traduire l’orientation stratégique de la gestion de produit en méthodes de travail concrètes et reproductibles. Vous créerez les modèles, les flux de travail, les normes, les automatisations, les tableaux de bord, la documentation et les expériences d’accompagnement qui aideront les gestionnaires de produit à appliquer ces pratiques dans leur travail quotidien.
 Vous travaillerez en collaboration avec les équipes de gestion de produits, de marketing de produits, de R-D, des ventes et des opérations afin de traduire les modèles opérationnels convenus en solutions claires, simples, mesurables et adoptées. La réussite ne se mesure pas uniquement à la production de documentation sur les processus. Elle se définit par la facilitation de l’adoption des méthodes de travail souhaitées, la réduction des tâches manuelles évitables, l’amélioration de la qualité et de la circulation de l’information, ainsi que par le soutien apporté aux équipes pour qu’elles utilisent de manière cohérente les outils et les processus sélectionnés.
 Votre journée en un coup d'oeil : 
 Mettre en œuvre la feuille de route des pratiques de gestion de produit définie par la direction de la gestion de produit, en traduisant les priorités en outils concrets, en flux de travail, en modèles, en lignes directrices et en plans de déploiement.
 Établir et maintenir des normes pratiques pour les activités essentielles de gestion de produit, notamment la documentation des problèmes du marché, la collecte d’informations sur les clients et le marché, les données de PLM vers les ordres d’achat, la mise à jour de la feuille de route, la réception des demandes, le triage, l’établissement des priorités et les transferts interfonctionnels.
 Configurer et améliorer les systèmes qui soutiennent ces pratiques, notamment SharePoint, Confluence, Azure DevOps, CRM, Wrike, Microsoft 365, Power Automate, les tableaux de bord et les flux de travail assistés par l’IA.
 Créer des modèles réutilisables, des listes de vérification, des exemples, des guides pratiques et des conseils en libre-service qui aident les gestionnaires de produit à appliquer les méthodes convenues avec moins d’ambiguïté et sans avoir à tout réinventer.
 Établir des structures d’information claires et des sources de référence pour les actifs de produit réutilisables, les connaissances sur le marché et les produits, les feuilles de route, les personas, les « tâches à accomplir » (Jobs-to-be-Done), les capacités et la documentation relative aux pratiques.
 Collaborez avec les gestionnaires de produit, les gestionnaires de marketing de produit, les responsables de produit, les responsables de la R-D et les intervenants commerciaux pour tester les flux de travail, cerner les points de friction et peaufiner les détails de mise en œuvre sans remettre en question les décisions stratégiques déjà prises.
 Favorisez l’adoption grâce à l’intégration, aux heures de consultation, à une formation concise, à des exemples, à des notes de mise à jour et à des communications ciblées sur le changement.
 S’assurer que les outils et les automatisations respectent les attentes de l’entreprise en matière de traitement de l’information, d’accès, de qualité, de traçabilité et de responsabilité humaine.
 À quoi ressemble la réussite? : 
 Les gestionnaires de produit consacrent moins de temps à des tâches de coordination évitables, à la recherche d’information, à la refonte de modèles et à la mise à jour manuelle des statuts.
 Les pratiques convenues se traduisent par des solutions opérationnelles et sont appliquées de manière cohérente par toutes les équipes.
 L’information échangée entre les équipes Produit, R-D, Marketing produit et Ventes est plus complète, mieux structurée et plus facile à exploiter.
 Les référentiels, les flux de travail, les tableaux de bord et les automatisations ont des responsables clairement identifiés et restent à jour après le lancement.
 L’adoption et la santé des processus sont visibles grâce à un petit ensemble de mesures fiables, et les améliorations sont fondées sur des données probantes.
 Les parties prenantes perçoivent ces pratiques comme un outil utile plutôt que comme une bureaucratie supplémentaire.
 Ce qui fait de vous un excellent candidat : 
 Expérience dans les domaines de l’exploitation des produits, des opérations d’affaires, de la gestion de programmes, de l’analyse d’affaires, de l’amélioration des processus ou dans un rôle similaire axé sur la mise en œuvre.
 Expérience avérée dans la traduction d’un modèle opérationnel convenu en flux de travail concrets, en outils, en modèles et en améliorations mesurables.
 Maîtrise pratique des plateformes de gestion des flux de travail et des connaissances telles qu’Azure DevOps, SharePoint, Confluence, Wrike, Microsoft Dynamics, Power Automate ou des outils comparables.
 Solides compétences en cartographie des processus et en analyse des exigences, avec la capacité d’identifier les intervenants, les intrants, les décisions, les transferts, les exceptions, les contrôles, les extrants et les mesures.
 Aisance à configurer des outils, à mettre en place des automatisations légères, à structurer des données et à créer des tableaux de bord ou des rapports.
 Communication écrite claire et capacité à produire des normes, des instructions, des exemples et du matériel de formation concis.
 Des compétences pratiques en gestion du changement, notamment en matière de pilotage, d’intégration, de collecte de rétroaction, d’accompagnement à l’adoption et d’amélioration itérative.
 Un esprit orienté service et le discernement nécessaire pour simplifier les processus, et non les alourdir.
 La capacité de travailler de manière transversale, de gérer un carnet de commandes et de faire avancer le travail sans s’appuyer sur une autorité formelle.
 Maîtrise du français et de l’anglais, tant à l’oral qu’à l’écrit (ce poste nécessite des interactions avec nos collaborateurs et clients internationaux)
 Un atout si vous avez :

Then Jobber might be the place for you! We’re looking for a Senior Solutions Engineer to be part of our Product Engineering & Partnerships ecosystem.

Jobber exists to help people in small businesses be successful. We work with small home service businesses, like your local plumbers, painters, and landscapers, to transform the way service is delivered through technology. With Jobber they can quote, schedule, invoice, and collect payments from their customers while providing an easy and professional customer experience. Running a small business today isn’t like it used to be—the way we consume and deliver service is changing rapidly, technology is evolving, and customers expect more. That’s why we put the power and flexibility in their hands to run their businesses how, where, and when they want! 

Our culture of transparency, inclusivity, collaboration, and innovation has been recognized by Great Place to Work, Canada’s Most Admired Corporate Cultures, and more. Jobber has also been named on the Globe and Mail’s Canada’s Top Growing Companies list, and Deloitte Canada’s Technology Fast 50™, Enterprise Fast 15, and Technology Fast 500™ lists. With an Executive team that has over thirty years of industry experience of leading the way, we’ve come a long way from our first customer in 2011—but we’ve just scratched the surface of what we want to accomplish for our customers https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EkfZmHrRLx4&list=PLoktA_D-2UEnxMLfCe93bANKXVXd2bdN8&index=24.

The team:

Our Senior Solutions Engineer will join a rapidly growing group integral to Jobber’s core strategy. This team plays a key role in expanding our software solutions to meet all our Service Providers needs. Our app marketplace is growing with interest from a variety of external partners of all stripes. You will work closely with our Partnerships group, specifically our Platform Experience Engineering team and our Business Development group. You’ll also work with external development teams of all shapes and sizes. All of these groups work hand in hand to get valuable integrations shipped and added to Jobber’s marketplace. 

At Jobber we never stop growing and learning, and you shouldn’t either. Through continuous 1:1’s, dedicated feedback and support from your manager and our Learning and Development team, and your own sense of curiosity, we hope you develop to another level with your skill set.

The role:

Reporting to the Senior Manager, Software Engineering, as a Senior Solutions Engineer you will leverage your expertise in application marketplaces and APIs to drive the success of our integration initiatives. You will work closely with both technical and non-technical teams, as well as leadership, to create impactful solutions to help our customers and their small businesses be successful. You will collaborate with the partnerships team and external partner groups to deeply understand their technical operational needs and translate those conversations into actionable engineering plans. You will work closely with cross-functional teams of engineers, designers, marketers, sales and leadership to bring these products to life and accelerate partner growth. 

We’re looking for people who are ready to solve problems that millions of entrepreneurs are facing, using their experience to influence both a product and our team, all the while still working on developing their own craft. At Jobber we never stop growing and learning, and you shouldn’t either. Through continuous 1:1s, dedicated feedback and support from your manager and our Learning and Development team, and your own sense of curiosity, we hope you develop to another level with your skill set.

As a Senior Solutions Engineer, you will:

 - Work with Business Development, Jobber Engineering and External Third Parties to propose and design solutions that meet all parties needs.  

 - Develop and implement integration strategies that enhance our application marketplace offerings.

 - Collaborate with cross-functional teams to design and optimize API solutions (REST and GraphQL).

 - Act as a liaison between technical teams and external stakeholders, ensuring clear communication and alignment on project goals.

 - Provide technical support and guidance to partners throughout the integration process.

 - Identify opportunities for innovation and process improvement within the integration landscape.

 - Collaborate closely with cross-functional teams to conceptualize, design, and iteratively deliver high-impact features that address customer needs

 - Partner with Product and Design teams to shape and define the strategic product roadmap

 - Actively participate in code reviews and testing processes to ensure code quality and maintainability

 - Champion the development of consistent engineering practices and reusable code solutions to enhance overall efficiency

 - Participate in discussions to drive consensus on optimal solutions for complex customer problems

 - Research, promote, and implement industry best practices within your team's domain, staying at the forefront of technological advancements

 - Effectively communicate complex technical concepts to diverse audiences, bridging the gap between technical and non-technical stakeholders

 - Provide mentorship and guidance to team members at all levels, fostering their professional growth and career development

To be successful, you should have:

 - Previous experience in a solutions engineering or similar role.

 - Proven experience in application marketplace development and management.

 - Strong knowledge of API technologies, including REST and GraphQL.

 - Strong communication skills 

 - Collaborative problem solving skills coupled with the ability to think on your feet

 - Demonstrated expertise in developing highly scalable, robust software solutions across multiple layers of the technology stack

 - Proven leadership experience championing complex, high-impact projects and serving as core contributor

 - Exceptional proficiency in software design, architecture, and coding, with a focus on maintainability and performance

 - Outstanding collaboration and communication skills, coupled with the ability to significantly amplify the team’s productivity and effectiveness through mentorship/coaching

 - Strong self-motivation and resourcefulness, with the capacity to independently identify and leverage necessary resources for project delivery and problem-solving

 - Ability to navigate ambiguity and prioritize tasks effectively in dynamic, fast-paced environments

 - Passionate commitment to continuous learning and professional growth, with a track record of staying current with emerging technologies and industry trends

It would be really great (but not a deal-breaker) if you had:

 - Exposure or experience in a tech leadership role

 - Experience with our development stack: React, React Native, TypeScript, GraphQL API layer, and Ruby on Rails on AWS.

 Set reasonable expectations for the customer, and educate them on the repair process

Client Success Specialist 
 Town Web · HeyGov · ClerkMinutes. Remote, Central US hours.
 About us 
 We make municipal software built for clerks: websites residents can use, forms and payments that replace stacks of paper, and meeting minutes drafted after every meeting. More than 1,300 local governments rely on us, from counties and cities to villages and towns. We have local government customers in almost every state in the U.S.
 Our clients are municipal clerks and the government teams around them. They keep city hall running and rarely get thanked for it. Your job is to make working with us the easy part of their week.
 The role 
 Our AI agent now answers repeatable, well-documented questions. What is left is the work that  only a person can do: own a client's problem from the first message to the confirmed fix, build a relationship a clerk trusts, and turn what you learn into better documentation and a better product.
 This is not a ticket-closing job. Think of a great 5-star hotel that puts slippers by the bed before you ask. We want a clerk to finish a conversation with you and tell the clerk in the next town about the great experience they had. If that takes three calls, take three calls.
 It is also a technical job. You will work with our developers every day. When something breaks, you work out where it lives before anyone else has to. Is the problem occurring on the events calendar on the client’s homepage, or is happening within the calendar of events widget that is embedded on a department page? Is the wrong speaker name showing up only in the transcript or is it showing up in the finished minutes? You reproduce it, write it up so a developer can act without a follow-up question, stay on it until it ships, and tell the client yourself.
 What you will do 
 Delight clients 
 Make every interaction feel personal, warm, and unhurried, especially for less technical users who would rather talk to a person than read a help article
 Step in when the AI agent or the documentation is not enough, and make sure the client feels heard and helped, not processed
 Treat client sentiment as the real measure of success, not ticket speed
 Look for small moments to go above and beyond, and share what works so it becomes how the whole team operates
 Own the problem from start to finish 
 Be the named person on an account when things go wrong: one owner, one plan, regular updates, until the client says it is fixed
 Step in early when an account shows strain (repeat tickets, a rough launch, a frustrated message) and run the recovery. Get on a call, write down what is open, set dates, follow through
 Make sure nothing sits untracked once it leaves the support queue
 Diagnose, then escalate 
 Work out which product and which layer an issue lives in before you hand it to a developer
 Reproduce it, capture the steps with screenshots or a recording, and file it in Linear with everything a developer needs
 Check on your open Linear issues, chase what is stuck, and confirm the fix with the client
 Use Claude, connected to our code repository, to trace where a behavior comes from. For small, well-understood fixes, draft the change for a developer to review
 Knowledge base and AI support 
 Inherit and maintain the help center for all of our products. It is what our AI agent (Fin, in Intercom) answers from
 Write and improve articles from real, recurring questions, on a weekly rhythm measured against live ticket volume
 Write troubleshooting guides that separate look-alike problems, so the next person, or Fin, can tell them apart
 Tune Fin: review where it failed, fix the article, and teach it to ask a clarifying question when a request could mean two things
 Record short training videos so clients can learn at their own pace
 Support and onboarding 
 Handle the conversations Fin cannot resolve across Town Web (websites), HeyGov (forms, payments, reservations, campaigns), and ClerkMinutes (agendas, transcripts, minutes)
 Help new clients through onboarding with the projects team so they reach value quickly
 Get on a call when a situation needs a human voice
 Account care 
 Build real relationships with your assigned accounts
 Understand what each client is trying to accomplish, what they use, what they do not know we offer, and where they will need help before they ask
 Run proactive, recurring check-ins instead of waiting for tickets. For example, reach out a few weeks after go-live to review how their forms are performing
 Use product usage data to spot clients who are not getting full value yet
 Spot opportunity 
 Tell clients about services they do not use yet (digital forms, payments, .gov domains, accessibility, training) without it feeling like a pitch
 Flag possible expansion and renewal opportunities to the sales team
 Training 
 Get clients to real proficiency with the product, not just past their immediate question
 Work with Product Managers to co-host webinars about new features, or training.
 Tools you will use : Intercom and Fin, Linear, Claude, our help center, screen recording, Zoom phone.
 How we work 
 Delight over deflection. The goal is happy, successful clients, not fewer conversations
 Ownership over routing. A hard case is yours until it is resolved
 Diagnose before you escalate. A developer should never have to ask what the client actually saw
 Documentation is the foundation everything else runs on, not an afterthought
 Teaching over ticket-closing. Proficiency, not just an answer

BONUS

OUR PHILOSOPHY
